title: Unify least-privilege policy defaults across composition roots
goal: Ensure M3, M4, M6, and M7 composition roots always inject an explicit least-privilege policy when callers omit one, and keep all execution boundaries aligned.
context: ModuleRuntime fails closed when its policy is absent, but composition roots still passed nil in some paths. M7 also used a default evaluator for ExecutionBoundary while passing nil to ModuleRuntime and M6Orchestrator. This task aligns policy injection and adds direct regression coverage without granting execution by default.
forbidden_changes: Do not make the default policy grant write, execute, network, or destructive capabilities.
Do not bypass policy, approval, capability, schema, or cancellation checks.
Do not alter app UI or Xcode project files.
Do not change explicit injected policy behavior.
acceptance_criteria: M3 injects DefaultPolicyEvaluator when the caller supplies no policy.
M4 injects DefaultPolicyEvaluator when the caller supplies no policy.
M6 resolves one policy and shares it with ModuleRuntime and M6Orchestrator.
M7 resolves one policy and shares it with ModuleRuntime, M6Orchestrator, and ExecutionBoundary.
Explicit caller-provided policies continue to be used unchanged.
Default policy remains least privilege and does not implicitly grant execute capability.
A regression test proves default M3 execution is denied.
A regression test proves default M4 execution is denied.
A regression test proves default M6 execution is denied.
A regression test proves default M7 execution is denied and required CI gates pass.
verification: Confirm Swift package tests + repository integrity, macOS Xcode iOS arm64 build/unsigned IPA, and validate-contract CI gates.
recovery: Revert this single logical commit if existing explicitly authorized execution paths regress; retain fail-closed behavior for missing or denied policy.
